newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt appoints top legal religious authority.
newsitem.headline: Egypt appoints top legal religious authority.

text.p: Egypt on Monday appointed an Islamic law professor as mufti, the country's highest religious authority, a presidential decree said.
It named Nasr Fareed Mohamed Wasel, an al-Azhar University professor, to the post vacant since Mohamed Sayyed Tantawi was appointed as head of al-Azhar six months ago.
Wasel, born in 1937, taught Islamic law at universities in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. He started his career as a prosecutor.
A mufti issues fatwas, or legal opinions, on issues ranging from family life to economic practice. He also gives final approval to death sentences.
